entries.name: W3C Trace Context
entries.status_notes: Standard HTTP headers and value formats for propagating distributed tracing context.
entries.relevance: Provides the most widely applicable starting point for linking one AI task across HTTP service boundaries.
entries.limitations: Propagation can stop or be regenerated at provider boundaries; it does not supply disclosure policy or proof of causality.

entries.name: W3C Trace Context Level 2
entries.status_notes: Adds trace/span ID generation considerations and a random trace-ID flag.
entries.relevance: Random-ID signalling and more explicit ID-generation rules may affect safe cross-domain correlation and sampling.
entries.limitations: Work in progress and not a final W3C Recommendation.

entries.name: W3C Baggage
entries.status_notes: Standard representation and propagation of application-defined properties associated with a distributed workflow.
entries.relevance: Could carry scoped correlation or policy hints that are not part of trace identity.
entries.limitations: High risk of sensitive-data leakage; requires strict allow-listing, size limits, and trust-boundary handling.

entries.name: OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions
entries.status_notes: Common meanings and names for telemetry attributes, spans, metrics, events, logs, and resources.
entries.relevance: A shared vocabulary is necessary to combine evidence produced by different implementations.
entries.limitations: Semantic compatibility does not guarantee context propagation, authorisation, retention, or topology mapping.

entries.name: OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions
entries.status_notes: Still unreleased. From 2026-10-14 through 2026-10-26 main narrowed MCP session-duration dimensions, clarified MCP JSON-RPC error attributes, made provider-supplied tool-call IDs conditionally required for execute_tool without synthetic fallbacks, changed inference counters to record only known positive contributions, and split embedding duration and input-token metrics from the generic inference metrics. Earlier October changes renamed inference metrics, covered failed operations, and promoted the input/output-bearing inference-details event to recommended.
evidence: inference duration, time-to-first-chunk, and output-chunk timing
dedicated embedding duration and per-operation input-token metrics
provider-supplied tool-call ID on execute_tool spans
MCP JSON-RPC error code and error type
MCP session duration without per-operation transport dimensions
stable main-agent entity and internal-span associations
agent-skill name, source, resource, and script attributes
cache-read, cache-write, and reasoning token subsets
recommended inference input and output details event
entries.relevance: Improves persistent-agent, skill-lifecycle, tool-to-conversation, sampling, error, failure-cost, embedding, latency, and payload correlation while distinguishing provider-issued tool identifiers, aggregate positive token contributions, and per-operation distributions.
entries.limitations: Experimental unreleased main, not a versioned release or stable cross-provider contract. Repeated metric renames, the new embedding-specific instruments, and the positive-only counter rule are incompatible with earlier collectors and can create apparent discontinuities. Omitted or zero token contributions are intentionally not recorded, so absence does not prove zero use; per-operation histograms remain distributions rather than totals or cost. Provider-issued tool-call IDs improve correlation but do not authenticate an actor, and implementations must not invent fallback IDs. The recommended operation-details event contains model inputs and outputs and needs explicit collection, access, retention, and redaction policy. Main-agent and skill fields remain development status; source URIs can expose internal names, paths, or credentials. No convention coordinates incident retention or proves identity across domains.

Inference operation-details event promoted to recommended, 2026-10-09
Agent-skill execute-tool attributes and span refinements, 2026-09-29
Aggregate and per-operation inference token metrics, 2026-09-22
Remove cache usage from internal invoke_agent spans, 2026-08-27

entries.name: Model Context Protocol trace context propagation
entries.version: Published 2026-07-28 specification; SEP-414 Final; Python SDK v2.3.0
entries.status_notes: The MCP project released the 2026-07-28 specification on 2026-07-28, and its versioning page identifies that version as current and ready for use. SEP-414 remains Final and documents W3C trace context and baggage in JSON-RPC _meta. The official Python SDK v2.3.0, released 2026-10-02, records peer JSON-RPC error responses on client OpenTelemetry spans with ERROR status, error.type, and rpc.response.status_code while leaving successful requests UNSET.
evidence: JSON-RPC error code and client-span status
entries.relevance: Provides a protocol-defined carrier for following agent-to-tool requests across MCP clients, servers, and gateways; the tagged Python SDK additionally makes protocol-error outcomes visible on the correlated client span.
entries.limitations: Published MCP project specification, not an IETF or W3C standard. SEP-414 defines conventions without requiring every implementation to propagate or emit them; SDK coverage and API stability vary. The v2.3.0 error-span behavior is Python-SDK-specific, and automatic discovery against a legacy server can intentionally produce one ERROR probe span when server/discover is unsupported. Correlation and error metadata still need trust-boundary, cardinality, and data-minimisation policy.

primary_sources.title: MCP SEP-414 trace context propagation conventions
Record JSON-RPC errors on client spans, 2026-10-02
MCP specification versioning and current version

entries.name: OpenMetrics 1.0
entries.status_notes: Stable metric exposition format with broad Prometheus ecosystem adoption.
entries.relevance: A common metric format can carry inference, compute, and network health evidence between collection systems.
entries.limitations: Aggregated time series often cannot explain the critical path of one transaction.

entries.name: OpenMetrics 2.0
entries.status_notes: Second-generation OpenMetrics work with improved alignment to the OpenTelemetry data model and naming conventions.
entries.relevance: Potentially improves interoperability between inference metrics, Prometheus systems, and OpenTelemetry.
entries.limitations: Experimental at baseline; compatibility and production adoption are not established.

entries.name: vLLM metrics, tracing, and per-request metrics
entries.status_notes: v0.32.0 is the latest tagged release. It ships the previously main-only prompt-token cache-source accounting and opt-in HiSparse host-block lifetime, idle-before-eviction, and reuse-gap histograms. The release also adds KV-fetch request counts by stage, admission-rejection and watermark-request metrics, custom histogram buckets, JSON log formatting, and per-session profiling controls. These are implementation signals rather than provider-neutral protocol semantics.
evidence: prompt tokens cached by device, host, disk, peer-to-peer, or external source
KV transport failure and expiry metrics
HiSparse host-block lifetime, idle-before-eviction, and reuse-gap histograms
entries.relevance: Separates inference-side queue, admission, execution, streaming, cache/offload, connector-failure, watermark, and speculative-decoding behavior that otherwise appear as one network-visible request time; released tier, fetch-stage, and lifecycle signals add evidence about where cached state came from and how it is retrieved and reused.
entries.limitations: Per-request timing remains opt-in through --enable-per-request-metrics, requires server statistics, and can add non-negligible CPU overhead; the HiSparse lifecycle histograms require --kv-cache-metrics. Metrics are omitted for multiple sequences and multi-generation Responses tool turns, and streaming delivery requires a final usage-bearing event. Cache, connector, admission, watermark, residency, and encoder metrics are implementation-specific and do not establish transferable state or cross-provider semantics. Custom buckets and optional signal enablement can make deployments incomparable. Speculative acceptance fields remain experimental, opt-in, and single-sequence. Timing, profiling, log, and cache evidence can expose workload characteristics and require access and disclosure controls.

Prompt-token cache source-tier metric, shipped in v0.32.0
HiSparse host-block lifecycle metrics, shipped in v0.32.0

entries.name: NVIDIA Triton metrics and tracing
entries.status_notes: Provides Prometheus request/GPU/cache metrics and per-request tracing using Triton or OpenTelemetry modes.
entries.relevance: Provides inference and accelerator evidence that can be correlated with task and network observations.
entries.limitations: Telemetry configuration, naming, sampling, retention, and visibility are deployment-specific.

entries.name: OpenConfig gNMI
entries.version: 0.11.0 in revision history; document header states 0.10.0
entries.status_notes: The March 2026 revision history adds v0.11.0, while the visible specification header still reports v0.10.0 and 0.10.x compatibility.
entries.relevance: Supplies detailed device and interface evidence needed to separate path/device degradation from compute delay.
entries.limitations: Local device paths and counters need topology and transaction mapping; the baseline source has an internal version inconsistency.

entries.name: YANG-Push
entries.status_notes: Subscription and push mechanisms for YANG datastore updates, including on-change notifications.
entries.relevance: Can publish modelled network and on-path telemetry without continuous polling.
entries.limitations: Data models, access control, topology mapping, and cross-domain correlation remain separate concerns.

primary_sources.title: RFC 8641: Subscription to YANG Notifications for Datastore Updates

entries.name: IP Flow Information Export (IPFIX)
entries.status_notes: Standards-track protocol for exporting traffic-flow information from exporters to collectors.
entries.relevance: Shows who communicated, when, and at what scale across network boundaries.
entries.limitations: Sampling and aggregation can obscure short incidents; flow identity does not establish application causality.

entries.name: BGP Monitoring Protocol (BMP)
entries.status_notes: Provides route views and BGP session monitoring; active work includes BMP v4/TLV and routing-event extensions.
entries.relevance: Can place routing changes on the same timeline as application and inference degradation.
entries.limitations: Temporal coincidence is not causal proof; visibility depends on where BMP is collected.

entries.name: STAMP and TWAMP
entries.status_notes: Active measurement protocols for one-way and round-trip performance metrics.
entries.relevance: Provides controlled path-performance evidence independent of application and inference instrumentation.
entries.limitations: Probe paths and treatment may differ from the transaction; one-way interpretation depends on time quality.

primary_sources.title: RFC 8762: Simple Two-Way Active Measurement Protocol

entries.name: In Situ OAM (IOAM)
entries.status_notes: Defines on-path operational and telemetry data fields for use inside limited IOAM domains, with direct-export and encapsulation extensions.
entries.relevance: Can produce fine-grained path evidence that complements active probes and device counters.
entries.limitations: Limited-domain model, deployment overhead, integrity, privacy, and cross-domain disclosure constraints.

entries.name: IETF Network Telemetry Framework
entries.status_notes: Taxonomy and framework covering telemetry acquisition, export, analysis, and techniques including active, passive, and hybrid measurement.
entries.relevance: Provides a standards-based map for the network portion of the observability landscape.
entries.limitations: Does not define a cross-domain task-correlation or disclosure protocol.

entries.name: On-Path Telemetry YANG Data Models
entries.status_notes: IETF working-group draft revised 2026-10-09. Revision -07 replaces the former combined ietf-on-path-telemetry module with separate ietf-altmark-telemetry and ietf-ioam-telemetry modules and distinct namespaces while retaining augmentation of the existing AltMark and IOAM models.
evidence: separate Alternate Marking and IOAM telemetry modules
Alternate Marking loss and delay data
IOAM trace, proof-of-transit, direct-export, and edge-to-edge data
entries.relevance: Makes selected on-path evidence available through model-driven telemetry and YANG-Push while separating the AltMark and IOAM namespaces and aligning both with their existing configuration models.
entries.limitations: Work in progress and limited to Alternate Marking and IOAM. The revision does not define cross-domain identifier scope, clock-quality metadata, task correlation, or disclosure policy. The earlier performance-metrics review that marked revision -05 not ready does not establish the readiness of -07.

primary_sources.title: On-Path Telemetry YANG Data Models, revision -07

entries.name: Computing-Aware Traffic Steering (CATS) Framework
entries.status_notes: Published as RFC 10053 on 2026-10-06 after IETF consensus. The framework combines network and computing-resource information when selecting a service instance and is scoped to one service provider.
entries.relevance: Directly overlaps the talk's hypothesis that live network and compute signals may influence inference placement.
entries.limitations: Informational framework rather than a Standards Track exchange protocol. Its single-provider scope and abstract metrics do not solve multi-provider observability, federation, task correlation, or disclosure policy.

primary_sources.title: RFC 10053: A Framework for Computing-Aware Traffic Steering

entries.name: CATS Problem Statement, Use Cases, and Requirements
entries.status_notes: Published as RFC 10054 on 2026-10-06 after IETF consensus. It defines the CATS problem, use cases, and requirements, including distributed AI inference, service-instance affinity, and agreement on the meaning of compute and network metrics.
entries.relevance: Makes distributed AI inference, stateful service affinity, and consistent metric interpretation explicit CATS requirements rather than informal implementation assumptions.
entries.limitations: Informational requirements document rather than a protocol or data model. It is scoped to a single CATS domain and does not bind steering decisions or service-instance state to a cross-domain task, causal timeline, or independently verified outcome.

primary_sources.title: RFC 10054: Computing-Aware Traffic Steering (CATS) Problem Statement, Use Cases, and Requirements

entries.name: State, Storage, and Compute Affinity for AI Agent Service Selection in CATS
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft posted 2026-10-06 with no formal IETF standing. It proposes requirements and abstract attributes for steering stateful AI-agent requests using state location, storage and compute affinity, retention and reuse characteristics, and model/runtime readiness.
evidence: model revision, precision, adapter, runtime, and accelerator readiness
retention, decay, budget, and reuse-group attributes
entries.relevance: Directly narrows the documented state-and-cache-affinity gap by distinguishing reusable agent state, its locality and lifetime, and compute environments capable of consuming it.
entries.limitations: Early individual proposal with no formal IETF standing, working-group adoption, wire protocol, encoding, data model, implementation, or interoperability evidence. It assumes a single CATS domain and does not define cross-provider state transfer, compatibility proof, task correlation, or disclosure policy for state metadata.

primary_sources.title: State, Storage, and Compute Affinity for AI Agent Service Selection in Computing-Aware Traffic Steering, revision -00

entries.name: CATS YANG Data Model
entries.status_notes: CATS working-group -00 approved and posted 2026-09-23, replacing draft-yl-cats-data-model. The Standards Track work defines an ietf-cats YANG module that augments ietf-routing with CATS base policy, traffic classifiers, service-instance metrics, operational counters, and limit notifications.
evidence: service-instance source, priority, affinity, and location
extensible service metric type and value
matched and forwarded packet and byte counters
entries.relevance: Provides a concrete model-driven mapping between CATS services, service instances, topology locations, steering inputs, and operational counters, directly narrowing the documented topology and service-mapping gap.
entries.limitations: Working-group draft, not an RFC, with no implementation or interoperability evidence found. It operates within the CATS framework's provider scope and does not map an AI task to a service instance across domains. Metric meanings depend on separate extensible definitions, and the model does not supply shared time quality, evidence integrity, or disclosure policy. Writable state can affect routing and readable state can reveal sensitive service and topology information.

primary_sources.title: Data Model for Computing-Aware Traffic Steering (CATS), revision -00
CATS data-model document history and working-group approval, 2026-09-23

entries.name: CATS OAM Framework
entries.status_notes: IETF working-group draft dated 2026-07-21 covering fault management and performance monitoring across clients, network paths, and service instances.
entries.relevance: One of the closest current standards efforts to joint network-and-compute causal evidence.
entries.limitations: Early work in progress; data models, cross-domain trust, and implementation experience remain open.

entries.name: CATS OAM Use Cases and Requirements
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft dated 2026-07-31; it has no formal IETF standing at baseline.
entries.relevance: Provides operator-oriented scenarios against which FOX and other cross-domain models can be tested.
entries.limitations: Individual draft, not IETF consensus; must be treated as a discovery source and working proposal.

primary_sources.title: CATS OAM Use Cases and Requirements

entries.name: Quality of Outcome (QoO)
entries.status_notes: IETF working-group document in advanced processing at baseline; defines application-specific network quality assessment and outcome scores.
entries.relevance: May help translate network measurements into an application-facing signal suitable for placement or troubleshooting.
entries.limitations: A quality score does not identify the causal component and may hide distribution or measurement assumptions.

entries.name: Transport Considerations for Large-Scale Distributed Inference Networks
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft dated 2026-07-04; it has no formal IETF standing at baseline.
entries.relevance: Directly addresses traffic generated by disaggregated and expert-parallel inference and may produce new measurement requirements.
entries.limitations: Early individual proposal focused largely on large-scale inference networks; it must not be presented as consensus or general WAN evidence.

primary_sources.title: Transport Considerations for Large-Scale Distributed Inference Networks

entries.name: Proxy Modes for Agent-Tool Protocols
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft published 2026-08-13 with no formal IETF standing. It proposes W3C trace propagation, append-only hop metadata, and intermediary metrics for agent-tool protocol proxies.
entries.relevance: Directly addresses observability across agent-tool intermediaries and makes routing, retry, partial-failure, and gateway-hop behaviour more visible.
entries.limitations: Early individual proposal with no IETF consensus or demonstrated interoperable implementation; its hop metadata may expose topology and requires integrity, privacy, and bounded-disclosure controls.

entries.name: Temporal Integrity Metadata (TIM) for Infrastructure Telemetry
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft dated 2026-08-08 and last updated 2026-08-10; it has no formal IETF standing. It proposes transport-agnostic metadata describing the temporal integrity of telemetry observations.
entries.relevance: Directly addresses the documented need to qualify timestamps from heterogeneous application, inference, and network evidence before constructing a causal timeline.
entries.limitations: Work in progress with no working-group adoption, consensus, transport binding, interoperability evidence, or known implementation. Quality is self-declared; the draft does not synchronise clocks, guarantee declared accuracy, or establish causal order, and integrity and disclosure policy remain deployment concerns.

primary_sources.title: Temporal Integrity Metadata (TIM) for Infrastructure Telemetry

entries.name: Scoping and Comparability Requirements for Exported Network Telemetry Identifiers
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft revised 2026-09-04; it has no formal IETF standing. Revision -01 substantially replaces the earlier vocabulary-centric structure with broader requirements for defining the scope and comparability of telemetry identifiers and statistics.
entries.relevance: Directly addresses semantic ambiguity that can cause collectors to merge unrelated records, compare incommensurate values, or construct invalid cross-domain evidence timelines.
entries.limitations: Work in progress with no working-group adoption, consensus, wire format, data model, implementation, or interoperability evidence. Revision -01 no longer defines the four named scope values or omitted-identifier default from -00; its abstract says scope and comparison conditions MUST be explicit while the requirements section says identifiers or statistics SHOULD define them, so normative strength remains uncertain. Declared scope also does not authenticate or independently verify identity, time, or integrity.

primary_sources.title: Scoping and Comparability Requirements for Exported Network Telemetry Identifiers

entries.name: Data Manifest for Contextualized Telemetry Data
entries.status_notes: IETF OPSAWG document revision -16, posted 2026-10-05, moved to IESG Evaluation::AD Followup on 2026-10-22 after the IESG ballot. The document has enough positions to pass once four DISCUSS positions are resolved; IANA reports actions needed, and automated YANG validation reports no errors or warnings.
entries.relevance: Makes YANG telemetry more defensible for later analysis by binding observations to the platform, schema, subscription, and collection conditions under which they were produced.
entries.limitations: Not yet approved or published as an RFC; four IESG DISCUSS positions require resolution, AD follow-up and IANA actions remain, and there is no current telechat date. The Platform Manifest and current-period augmentation are normative, but the Data Collection Manifest remains a non-normative example because YANG lacks design-time schema mount. Data lineage, task correlation, cross-domain disclosure policy, and proof that metadata is accurate are out of scope.

primary_sources.title: A Data Manifest for Contextualized Telemetry Data, revision -16
Data Manifest document history, IESG ballot, and review activity

entries.name: Agent Run Metrics
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft revised 2026-10-05 with no formal IETF standing and retargeted for Independent Submission as Informational. Revision -01 removes proposed standards-tree media types and registries, uses application/json and application/json-seq with prefix-based extension values, adds an implementation-status section, and corrects the cache-write cost-share example.
evidence: timing, status, termination, and error metadata
W3C trace ID and span ID bindings
entries.relevance: Directly addresses the documented need for retry and delegation lineage and offers a candidate vocabulary for joining per-run agent activity to distributed traces without including prompts, completions, tool arguments, or tool results.
entries.limitations: Early individual proposal with no IETF consensus, working-group adoption, conforming report emitter, or interoperability evidence. The draft identifies research analysis scripts and contextburn 0.2.1, but neither emits the proposed report format; contextburn implements only related derived quantities. Reports remain reporter assertions rather than independently verified consumption evidence, and signatures, provider reconciliation, and authentication mechanisms are out of scope. Counters and persistent run identifiers can disclose sensitive activity patterns.

entries.name: BMP Statistics Information TLV
entries.status_notes: IETF GROW working-group draft revised 2026-09-11. Revision -01 changes the proposed wire layout with measurement-window duration, sample count, and microsecond-resolution extrema timestamps; it adds percentile entries and constrains interpretation to gauge statistics.
evidence: snapshot, mean, median, and percentile statistics
entries.relevance: Can preserve short routing-state excursions between exports and make statistical comparison assumptions explicit.
entries.limitations: Not an RFC; incompatible draft wire changes and no implementation evidence found. Comparisons require compatible collection settings; the draft does not export collection methodology or mandate a percentile algorithm. Unsigned exporter assertions and sensitive router dynamics require integrity, access, and disclosure controls.

primary_sources.title: BMP Statistics Information TLV, revision -01 dated 2026-09-11

entries.name: STAMP IP and IPv6 Extension Header Reflection
entries.status_notes: IETF IPPM working-group draft revised to -25 on 2026-10-22 and is in IESG Evaluation::AD Followup for Proposed Standard. The ballot has enough positions to pass once remaining issues are resolved, and IANA marks the version changed and requiring review. The late revisions specify IPv4, IPv6, and UDP header handling, add STAMP session-state notifications and rate limiting for all STAMP sessions, and refine MTU, operational, and security behavior. If approved, the document updates RFC 8762.
evidence: reflected IPv4 and IPv6 extension headers
IPv4, IPv6, and UDP header handling
rate limiting for all STAMP sessions
entries.relevance: Connects active probes with selected on-path header evidence and now specifies session-state notification and rate-limiting behavior; IESG Evaluation makes this a late-review candidate rather than an early draft.
entries.limitations: Not approved or published as an RFC; AD follow-up and IANA re-review remain, and three IPR disclosures are listed. The cited Teaparty commit targets revision -04, so current -25 conformance is not established. Limited-domain use, header disclosure, reflection amplification, data-plane access, rate-limit configuration, and MTU constraints remain deployment concerns.

entries.name: Agent Operation Continuity Across Executor Replacement
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft published 2026-09-15 with no formal IETF standing. It proposes continuity requirements for operation identity, immutable provider bindings, attempt evidence, unresolved outcomes, and stale-executor fencing.
entries.relevance: Addresses evidence loss and unsafe reinterpretation when an agent executor fails or is replaced.
entries.limitations: One authoritative coordination domain only; no universal identifier, evidence format, or cross-domain ledger migration. The draft reports same-team local and synthetic-provider testing, not live-provider deployment or independent interoperability. Provider assertions do not prove outcomes; persistent identifiers and request digests need minimisation, access, and retention controls.

primary_sources.title: Agent Operation Continuity Across Executor Replacement, 2026-09-15

entries.name: AI Audit Reference Architecture for Post-Hoc Agent Accountability
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft revision -01 dated 2026-09-21; it has no formal IETF standing. The revision adds confirmation windows, live parent-credential revalidation, explicit producer-unavailability policy, independently observed effects, audience binding, a separately redactable content container, and a sixth verification check, while expanding security and completeness gaps.
evidence: signed log commitments and external registration
verified, accepted, bound, existence, coverage, and ordering checks
producer failure and out-of-band anomaly handling
entries.relevance: Addresses the trust, integrity, and recipient-disclosure gaps in post-hoc cross-organisational evidence.
entries.limitations: Reference architecture, not a deployed exchange protocol or real-time authorisation mechanism. The author reports informal sample-code testing, but no published implementation, formal model, or interoperability evidence was found. Revision -01 explicitly leaves declared-scope evasion, tail truncation and same-length forks, confirmation-window sizing, human-authority bootstrapping, observer compromise, denial of service, and formal verification unresolved. Signatures still cannot establish completeness or outcome truth.

primary_sources.title: AI Audit Reference Architecture for Post-Hoc Agent Accountability, revision -01 dated 2026-09-21

entries.name: Audit Record Format for AI Agent Authorization Decisions
entries.status_notes: A replacement individual Internet-Draft was posted 2026-10-16 and explicitly archives draft-gilda-wimse-agent-audit-record-02; it has no formal IETF standing. The replacement defines 17 required predicate members and one optional member, adds evaluation-input freshness and anchor rules, retains decision/effect checks, and maps the record to proposed AUDIT work. The companion agent-evidence-vectors v0.26.0 release on 2026-10-26 rewrites the audit corpus for the replacement draft and expands it to 111 cases with Go and Python verification paths.
evidence: agent, delegation, resource, and request binding
17 required and one optional predicate members
evaluated versus not-evaluated status and unavailable inputs
agree, disagree, not-exercised, and indeterminate outcomes
entries.relevance: Supplies a concrete candidate record and verification algorithm for correlating authorization decisions with independently observed effects across a service boundary; the replacement draft tightens evaluation-input and anchoring semantics, and the tagged corpus makes its syntax and verdict rules executable rather than only prose.
entries.limitations: Replacement individual proposal with no working-group adoption, IETF consensus, independent interoperability result, or proof that the companion verifiers are complete; Datatracker lists two IPR disclosures. Legacy -02 records lack the new evaluation.inputs structure and are malformed under -00; v0.26.0 rewrites 69 of 70 retained corpus members, removes one, adds cases, and requires consumers to re-pin file IDs using ID-MAP. The predicate URI and companion corpus are author-controlled and unregistered with IANA. A claimed observation vantage or human actor is not self-proving, a producer can withhold whole records, and a valid signature or internally coherent record does not prove completeness or external truth. Identifiers, paths, oversight records, and timing can disclose sensitive activity.

primary_sources.title: An Audit Record Format for AI Agent Authorization Decisions, replacement revision -00
Agent evidence vectors v0.26.0 release with the 111-case replacement-draft corpus, 2026-10-26

entries.name: OpenTelemetry Correlation Extension for Agent Action Capsules
entries.status_notes: The individual Internet-Draft remains revision -00 with no formal IETF standing. It defines the namespaced org.agentactioncapsule.otel payload block and advisory aac.capsule_id reverse join. Since the previous baseline, capsule-emit shipped Python 0.9.1 through 0.13.0, TypeScript 0.3.1, and Rust 0.0.8. Python 0.13.0 changes the default ledger to a store directory, refuses new flat JSONL ledgers while retaining migration commands, writes cross-stream confirms links into references[], and requires Agent Action Capsule 0.12.0 or later with its shared verifier.
evidence: trace ID and span ID or their deployment-policy digests
parent span ID and trace flags
allow-listed OpenTelemetry GenAI attributes with pinned semantic-convention source
entries.relevance: Proposes an explicit two-way join between active OpenTelemetry traces and signed, content-addressed agent-action evidence while defining disclosure tiers and a strict attribute allow-list; tagged multi-language emitter and verifier work improves the deployability of the underlying capsule records.
entries.limitations: Individual proposal with no working-group adoption, formal IETF standing, interoperability result, or OpenTelemetry registry acceptance. The tagged emitter and shared verifier validate base Agent Action Capsules, not this OpenTelemetry extension's namespaced payload or reverse-join semantics, and the separate base profile still has not standardised placement. Python 0.13.0 is a storage-format migration: new flat ledgers are refused and callers must use import/export tooling. The block is informational to verification and does not prove that the action occurred; a same-producer span is not independent corroboration. Trace and span identifiers can be lookup keys into user-bearing systems, so clear disclosure is conditional. Tier-2 conformance-registry structure remains unsettled.

primary_sources.title: OpenTelemetry Correlation Extension for Agent Action Capsules, revision -00

entries.name: Per-Call Proof for Local Tool Invocation by AI Agents
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft dated 2026-10-12 with no formal IETF standing. It proposes a Call Authority that evaluates policy and issues short-lived, single-use proofs bound to a JSON Canonicalization Scheme and SHA-256 digest of an MCP tools/call method, tool name, and arguments for verification at the tool server.
entries.relevance: Introduces a concrete candidate for binding a local tool invocation to a prior authorization decision without embedding the full arguments in the proof, narrowing the local tool-policy and auditable-decision gaps.
entries.limitations: Early individual proposal with no formal IETF standing, working-group adoption, implementation, interoperability result, trace binding, IANA registry, or finished reference repository; its implementation section says development is in progress and the repository is TBD. The Call Authority becomes a trust and availability dependency. Digest-bound arguments may be guessable, proof formats are profiles rather than fixed here, and the current MCP binding covers only tools/call.

primary_sources.title: Per-Call Proof for Local Tool Invocation by AI Agents, revision -01

entries.name: Rule Provenance for Autonomous AI Agent Audit Records
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft dated 2026-10-11 with no formal IETF standing and intended Experimental status. It profiles provenance records for the rules and policy snapshots applied to agent decisions, records the contemporaneous decision separately from later human override, and proposes independent-recorder receipts and public anchoring.
evidence: rule identifier, version, author, and approver
entries.relevance: Adds candidate evidence for which policy and rule versions produced a decision and for distinguishing the original machine decision from subsequent oversight, directly narrowing the provenance portion of the audit gap.
entries.limitations: Early individual proposal with no formal IETF standing, working-group adoption, implementation, independent interoperability, or proof that every relevant rule and action was recorded. Appendix C vectors were generated by a short script, not a deployed verifier. In-path and recorder-independence claims can be self-asserted, public anchoring does not establish semantic truth, and policy records may expose sensitive controls.

entries.name: AER-1 Portable Execution Receipt
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft revision -26 was posted 2026-10-22 and has no formal IETF standing. It specifies portable, independently checkable tool-call receipts over canonical request and result bytes, tool and caller scope, provenance class, a stable public verification URL, and workflow aggregation through Merkle roots and job hash chains. The author reports a deployed reference service and an open conformance kit with seven language runners, 124 vectors, and 127 checks per runner.
evidence: 124 conformance vectors across seven language runners
entries.relevance: Offers a concrete candidate receipt for carrying tool-execution evidence across implementation and organisational boundaries, including aggregation into a verifiable workflow trail.
entries.limitations: Individual proposal with no working-group adoption, IETF consensus, or independent standards status. The public service, draft, conformance kit, and reported interoperability evidence are operated or reported by the same author, so independent deployment remains unverified. A receipt proves the recorded canonical bytes and signature, not that the claimed external-world action occurred or completed correctly. Stable public URLs and repeated identifiers can expose or link activity, and operators still need disclosure, retention, and availability policy.

entries.name: Agent Execution Evidence
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft posted 2026-10-19 with no formal IETF standing and intended Standards Track status. It profiles SCITT Signed Statements for agent identity, capabilities, assessment, and supervision; hash-chains every-call evidence; defines receiver admission records, cross-operator linked records, and offline verification bundles. The cited Sijil prototype records decision points, tasks, refusals, approvals, and a signed hash chain, but does not yet export this draft's encoding.
evidence: tasks, refusals, approvals, and decision points
entries.relevance: Proposes an integrity-preserving evidence layer spanning agent admission, every-call execution, and cross-operator verification, directly addressing identity, retry lineage, and audit gaps.
entries.limitations: Individual proposal with no working-group adoption, IETF consensus, conforming implementation, or interoperability result. The cited prototype does not export the proposed encoding and lacks multiple draft features, including COSE signing, epochs, bundles, SCRAPI registration, per-call signatures, identity-validity and assurance checks, admission records, and cross-call linking. Some components use a Business Source License while the verifier and rule packs are open. Common scope representation, supervision and trust lists, and registries remain open issues. Signed chains do not prove record completeness or external outcome truth.

entries.name: Evidence Binding for AI Agent Credentials
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft posted 2026-10-19 with no formal IETF standing and intended Informational status. It maps the Agent Identity Management System minimum fields to Agent Execution Evidence, defines an aee_evidence credential claim binding a persistent agent, policy, evidence service, and optional assurance, and proposes admission-time checking, an AEE-Caller-Ref HTTP field, and actor/principal delegation chains.
entries.relevance: Provides a candidate bridge between agent credentials and the evidence service and transaction used to verify execution, narrowing the identity-to-audit correlation gap.
entries.limitations: Individual informational proposal with no working-group adoption, IETF consensus, implementation-status section, reference implementation, or interoperability evidence. It depends on the separate Agent Execution Evidence draft and proposed registries. Persistent logical identifiers and repeated policy digests permit cross-transaction linkability; the HTTP field reveals the evidence service and transaction to intermediaries and operators even though it carries no prompt or tool content. Credential binding does not establish that evidence is complete or truthful.

entries.name: Federated Observability Exchange (FOX)
entries.status_notes: Project hypothesis for neutral, policy-controlled exchange of selected cross-domain evidence.
entries.relevance: Explores whether neutral interconnection can address the coordination gap left by domain-local observability tools.
entries.limitations: No protocol, implementation, deployment, or independent validation exists at baseline.
